subject: Velocity.ai: rehost cost comparison and price-match proposal
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Dalton <mike.dalton@velocity.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal — price-match option + migration tradeoffs

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, youre evaluating a replacement and want to understand whether we can match their headline economics while also limiting migration risk. I put together a short comparison (attached) that shows two paths:

1) Price-match offer: match the incumbent effective unit rate for 12 months with staged credits for onboarding; Redwood remains on the hosted plane for the pilot and then transitions to a dedicated pool if you commit.
2) Rehost/replatform: one-time migration credit + implementation SOW; lower long-run unit cost but requires 8–12 weeks of integration and a runway for data migration.

Key asks for us to tighten the proposal:
- Confirm target headline effective rate (USD/token) youre comparing against (I used the number from your RFP callout).
- Any must-have integrations (VPC peering, KMS) for go/no-go?
- Who on your side will own procurement/legal and the timeline for execution?

Ive attached a short risk matrix and a draft pilot SOW we can run concurrently with contract negotiation to speed up go-live. If it helps, Lauren can run a brief TCO snapshot showing token-run assumptions vs your telemetry.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Wednesday (5/13) afternoon to walk through the spreadsheet?

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_velocity_price-match-proposal.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
Attachment: rehost-risk-matrix.pdf (PDF, 340KB)

From: Mike Dalton <mike.dalton@velocity.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Ruiz <emma@velocity.ai>, Sourcing Team <procure@velocity.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — price-match option + migration tradeoffs

Ava —

Appreciate the clear framing. A few quick notes:

• Headline rate: the incumbent is at $0.0009 / token effective after committed-volume credits.
• Integrations: VPC peering is required, KMS optional but preferred.
• Timeline: procurement will need ~3 weeks to process an initial PO; legal prefers contract language that includes rollback protections and an agreed-upon staged go-live.

Wed like to see: a) a price-match sheet that nets to $0.0009 effective for the pilot term, and b) a migration-risk summary with concrete rollback triggers. Please also include your SOC 2 and data residency evidence in the packet so Procurement can start an initial review.

Im available Wed 5/13 3–4pm PT for the call.

-Mike
Mike Dalton
Head of Platform Engineering 
Velocity.ai
Attachment: incumbent_pricing_snapshot.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood proposal — price-match option + migration tradeoffs

Ava/Team —

Nice thread. A few internal notes ahead of tomorrow's call:

- Price-match mechanics: recommend we offer a 12-month "effective rate" guarantee that combines a reduced per-token rate + an onboarding credit bucket. That keeps our list price intact and caps short-term revenue impact. See the attached workbook for scenarios.
- Migration risk: provide an explicit rollback SLA tied to KV-cache parity and a staged traffic split (10/30/60) over 4 weeks. Add a clause for temporary fallback to a compatible model-family in region if performance regression > 10% on latency P50.
- Commercial concession: propose a one-time implementation credit up to $45k for migration, tied to milestone delivery and a demo/QA signoff.
- Compliance evidence: procurement will ask for SOC2 type II and a short audit summary. I can pull the cert pack (Connor to attach).

Lauren — can you prepare a one-pager TCO showing run-rate at both the incumbent token rate and the rehosted long-run rate? Put in sensitivity on 20%/40% higher usage.

Ava — call scheduled for 2026-05-13 15:00 PT (invite sent). Ill be on for the call and can walk the risk matrix.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Attachment: pilot-sow-draft.docx (Word, 65KB)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Dalton <mike.dalton@velocity.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Sourcing Team <procure@velocity.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — price-match option + migration tradeoffs

Hi Mike / team —

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciate the candid tradeoff conversation. Inline notes and next steps below:

- Pricing: well drop the per-token pilot effective rate to $0.00088 (net of a $60k onboarding credit amortized over the 12-month pilot) so the math nets slightly below your incumbent while preserving a path to our standard list pricing after the pilot. Spreadsheet attached.
- Migration guardrails: we agreed to staged traffic split with rollback triggers at 10% model-quality regression or 15% latency increase P50 vs baseline. Well add the fallback model-family clause to the MSA.
- Procurement packet: Connor attached SOC2 type II summary, data-residency attestations, and a short implementation timeline.

Next steps:
1) We will send a redline-friendly term sheet by EOD Monday with the price-match mechanics and rollback language.
2) Youll loop in Procurement for the PO process; well provide the final packet for their review.
3) Lauren will share the TCO snapshot separately so you can evaluate run-rate scenarios.

If anything else comes up in Procurement, ping me directly — happy to expedite.

Appreciate the partnership — look forward to progressing this.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0138
